statement_en:
Let $f(x)$ be a nonnegative locally integrable nonincreasing function on $[1,+\infty)$, and suppose
$$\int_1^{+\infty}f(x)\,dx=+\infty.$$ Then the integral
$$\int_{1}^{+\infty}\min\{f(x),\frac{1}{x^p}\}\,dx$$
satisfies:
1. it diverges for $0<p\leq 1$;
2. it converges for $p>1$.
final_code:
import Mathlib

theorem min_trunc_integral_behavior
    {f : ℝ → ℝ}
    (h_nonneg : ∀ x ∈ Set.Ici (1 : ℝ), 0 ≤ f x)
    (h_antitone : AntitoneOn f (Set.Ici (1 : ℝ)))
    (h_locInt : ∀ b : ℝ, 1 ≤ b → IntervalIntegrable f volume 1 b)
    (h_diverge : Filter.Tendsto (fun b : ℝ => ∫ x in 1..b, f x) Filter.atTop Filter.atTop) :
    (∀ p : ℝ, 0 < p → p ≤ 1 →
        Filter.Tendsto
          (fun b : ℝ => ∫ x in 1..b, min (f x) (1 / Real.rpow x p))
          Filter.atTop
          Filter.atTop) ∧
    (∀ p : ℝ, 1 < p →
        ∃ L : ℝ,
          Filter.Tendsto
            (fun b : ℝ => ∫ x in 1..b, min (f x) (1 / Real.rpow x p))
            Filter.atTop
            (nhds L)) := by
  sorry
